$comment: VERSIONED CONTENT, NOT CODE (Carl, 4 Sep 2026; hard rule 14). WHAT A VISIT NEEDS SIGNING — the question the PMS must never answer for us. An arrival says who walked in and which provider they are here to see; whether that visit needs a first enduring agreement, an episodic pre-agreement, or nothing at all is decided HERE and the version below travels with the record the decision produced. If the PMS said 'enduring' and we obeyed, we would have hardcoded the very mapping versioning exists to prevent (TODO.md 'Reception-centric' section 2, named test arrival_type_is_decided_by_the_rule_set_not_the_pms). THIS IS NOT s 65C VALIDATION. The rules engine in apps/rules is a human-authored zone and validates the PARTICULARS of an agreement that already exists; this table decides which agreement to draft in the first place — a domain eligibility question, asked before there is any payload to validate. ROWS ARE EVALUATED IN FILE ORDER AND THE FIRST MATCH WINS, so order is meaning: coverage is checked before eligibility, because a patient already covered is asked for nothing whatever the provider is. A row matches when every key in its `when` equals the input of that name; a `when` with no keys matches everything, and the LAST row must be one so that every possible input reaches a decision. HARD RULE 6 IS ROWS 1, 2 AND 5. Enduring agreements are per practitioner x patient and GP-only (REQ-END-01/-01a): there is deliberately no input here for practice-wide coverage, so no edit to this file can make an enduring agreement cover a practice. A non-GP provider can never reach the `enduring` row. Treatment Plan Assignment, which REQ-END-01a offers specialists and allied health instead, is out of v1 scope — a non-GP therefore lands on `episodic_pre` for now, which asks the patient for the visit in front of them and asserts nothing about a plan. NOT HERE: the display words. What reception is told about a decision lives in the string table keyed by `key` (REQ-LANG-01). AN `enduring` ROW MUST NAME ITS PATHWAY. reg 65CA/65CB requires one and the draft is refused without it, so 'a GP practice, therefore MyMedicare' is a regulatory inference that belongs here where it is versioned and editable rather than buried in a switch. `accho_ams` is deliberately not selectable: it anchors to an ORGANISATION rather than the provider an arrival names (Addendum v3 section 1.1). Bump `version` on every edit.
$postServiceComment: THE SECOND MOMENT, ON THE SAME TABLE (Carl, 11 Sep 2026; TODO.md 'Two front doors' decision (b)). The patient has seen the practitioner, the service is known — its date (D5) and its MBS item numbers (D6b, REQ-REG-01; s 65C(4) table item 6) — and something must decide whether they are asked to sign again at the desk. IT IS A SEPARATE TABLE, NOT MORE ROWS ON THE ONE ABOVE, because it is asked at a different moment and its inputs are different facts: the pre-service table knows nothing about a billed item, and this one knows nothing about whether the practice offers ongoing agreements. Merging them would mean a `when` key that is meaningless on half the rows. ORDER IS MEANING HERE TOO: the first match wins and the last row must match everything. `covered` MEANS THE PATIENT DOES NOTHING. A signed pre-agreement for this patient, this practitioner and this day already assigns the benefit for the service in front of them, so a second signature would collect a second consent for one service (TODO.md 'One signature per episodic visit, not two'). THE CONTAINMENT CHECK IS DEFERRED, DELIBERATELY AND VISIBLY. 'Is the billed item INSIDE the pre-agreement's Basic Service Description' cannot be answered until the REQ-REG-03 mapping of MBS items to descriptions exists — it is the quarterly MBS Online ingest, a Phase-0/1 job (CONSULTATION-CAPTURE-PLAN section 3.1, 'blocked'). Until it does, a signed pre-agreement for the practitioner x patient x day counts as covering the service, which is the behaviour that plan records; `itemInsidePreAgreementDescription` is NOT an input here because an input nothing can compute is a lie in a rule table. `covered_by_enduring` IS ITS OWN ANSWER rather than a second `covered`, because the two have different consequences the reason code must not blur: an ongoing agreement's claim carries a reg 89AA notice, which is the CLAIM's business, one-way and never chased (hard rule 7, REQ-END-05, REQ-CHASE-02) — nothing in this table starts one. NO AMOUNT, ANYWHERE (hard rule 4): the inputs are booleans and the answer is a word.
